opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: R&D — designing new analog and embedded chips; up from $527M a year ago, growing far slower than revenue.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and the back office (SG&A); up from $485M a year ago.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent above the $36.24 kept as profit.
footerNote: Segment operating profit: Analog $1,992M, Embedded Processing $168M, Other $150M.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: in Q2, incl. $549M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds

oneTimers: Earnings per share included a 5-cent benefit that was not in the company's original guidance, as stated in the release.
Free cash flow of $2,738M includes $549M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds received in the quarter; a further $301M of CHIPS investment tax credits was used to reduce income taxes payable.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was $69M, less $141M of interest and debt expense — a net $72M expense outside operations.

segments.name: Analog
segments.note: Analog chips — sensing and power products used in nearly every electronic device; growth led by industrial, data center and automotive.

segments.name: Embedded Processing
segments.note: Processors that sit inside cars, appliances and factory equipment.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: DLP products, calculators and custom chips.

takeaways.text: Analog revenue rose 26% to $4.37B with broad growth led by industrial, data center and automotive demand — TI's biggest business did the heavy lifting.
takeaways.title: Analog is driving the quarter

takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 61.4% (from 57.9% a year ago) as revenue grew 23% while R&D and SG&A barely rose — operating profit jumped 48%.
takeaways.title: Margins expanded sharply

takeaways.text: TI returned $1,322M to owners in the quarter — $1,295M of dividends and $27M of buybacks; trailing-12-month free cash flow was $6.5B.
takeaways.title: Cash returned to owners

verdict: Texas Instruments' revenue rose 23% to $5.46B as Analog sales surged 26%, and flat running costs turned that growth into a 53% jump in net income to $1.98B.
